items.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: There was Jimmy Campbell on drums, Vince Guaraldi on piano, Bill Harris on trombone, and Nat Adderley and Charlie Byrd and myself.

ctx.x: Yeah. When I left Dinah, because my wife and I had a son and I said well I’ve got to try domesticated life. And so I went to Washington in October of ‘56 and I started working at a club that had just opened up in January and they had a house trio and they were bringing in names on the weekends. They brought in, the first one was I think it was Lucky Thompson, and then Art Farmer, and Donald Byrd, Gene Ammons, you know they’d bring them in for maybe one or two weekends. And they went down the list of all these…

intermission. And the deal went down with whoever was in charge at that club, so they were looking at another club and he said, “well look I have a little restaurant up on 18th and Columbia Road, why don’t you work with the trio up there and you can get back together for that” pending that this big club was going to open. And the deal fell through, and by that time we were starting to build up something going up there, so then we just stayed there. And then it just kept on escalating and getting better and…
That’s great you got to see, you know, a good part of the world.
